title: Eisenhower matrix
src: Dwight D. Eisenhower, 1954 speech, popularized by Stephen Covey
idea: Sort tasks by urgent and important. The important but not urgent box is where your best work lives.
apply: Draw four boxes tonight and place tomorrow's tasks. Block calendar time for the important, not urgent box before the day fills up.
remind: Urgent is loud. Important is quiet. Protect the quiet.
who: Jordan, a project manager with a loud Monday.

scenes.nar: Jordan is a project manager with four tasks on his Monday list, and every one of them feels urgent.
He answers whatever is loudest. The quarterly roadmap, the work that matters most, keeps sliding to next week.
Now he sorts first. The bug goes in do now. The roadmap goes in plan, with a calendar block. The email goes to a teammate. The drive gets dropped.

scenes.sub: It had a protected block, so it got done.
scenes.nar: By Thursday the roadmap is done, before anyone had to ask for it.
